messages:
katie: Heads-up: after the new client-side header normalization landed, a few customers report quota hits on the fallback model despite traces showing route=fastpath.

omar: Any sample? Id look at header canonicalization + our router matcher.

katie: Minimal repro: 

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer AAA' \\\
  -H 'X-Route: fastpath' \\\
  -d '{"input":"ping"}'
```

li: Replayed span id span-8c4. Gateway received header as "x-route" lowercase. Our fast-path map lookup is case-sensitive for perf.

omar: I remember we added lowercasing to ts-client to collapse duplicate headers. That explains it.

katie: Console shows routehint=fastpath but billing shows charged_pool=fallback-2.

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: tolerant-router-lookup -> canary by li at 6177777810

omar: Short plan: (1) revert client header lowercasing in next patch (py/ts) (2) add case-insensitive fallback in gateway and emit metric routing.header_case_fallback (3) add console tile surfacing route vs billed pool by tenant.

li: I'll do the gateway change and a unit test. Will also add the metric and a log line when fallback used.

katie: I'll cut the python revert PR and update the changelog to clarify header guarantees. Can someone own TS?

omar: I'll own TS patch and release. Also will add an integration e2e test that runs client->gateway->router to catch this in CI.

dev-bot: Canary deploy started: tolerant-router-lookup (3 instances) at 6177777822

li: Dashboard idea: quick tile showing tenants with mismatch_count > 0 in last 24h. Add an alert at >0.1%.

katie: TL;DR: revert normalization -> release client patches; deploy tolerant-gateway lookup canary now; add metric and dashboard; monitor 48h. Tagging @omar @li.

omar: Thanks. Once patches land we should publish a short note in release notes explaining header handling to avoid confusion.
